tasks.description: Return the sum of the even numbers in the list.
Return the words of the text in reverse order, joined by single spaces. Words are separated by single spaces.
Return true when the text reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case.
Count the vowels (a, e, i, o, u, either case) in the text.
Return the FizzBuzz text for n: "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5, "FizzBuzz" for both, else the number.
Return the largest number in the list, or none when it is empty.
Return how many times each word appears in the text (words separated by single spaces), as a map from word to count.
Parse the text as a whole number and return it doubled. When it isn't a number, fail with the error BadInput, defined as `type BadInput = NotANumber(text: String)`.
Return n factorial (n is 0 or more, at most 20).
Return the nth Fibonacci number, with fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1.
Return the words sorted by length, shortest first; words of the same length keep their order.
Return the list without repeated numbers, keeping the first time each appears.
Given the record `type Rect { width: Float  height: Float }`, return the total area of the rectangles.
Given `type Shape = Circle(radius: Float) | Square(side: Float)`, return the shape's area; use 3.14 for pi.
Return the index of the first negative number in the list, or none when there is none.
Shift each lowercase letter a to z forward by k places in the alphabet, wrapping from z to a; other characters stay the same. k is 0 to 25.
Return the transpose of the matrix (a list of rows, all the same length, at least one row).
The list is sorted ascending. Return the index of target, or none when it isn't there.
Return a divided by b, or fail with `type MathError = DivideByZero` when b is 0.
Group the words by their first letter: a map from the letter (as text) to the words starting with it, in their order. No word is empty.
Return the running totals of the list: each item is the sum of the items up to and including it.
Return the greatest common divisor of two positive whole numbers.
Capitalize the first letter of each word (words separated by single spaces) and lowercase the rest.
Return true when n is a prime number.
Return the prime numbers below n, smallest first.
Return the sum of the decimal digits of n (n is 0 or more).
Run-length encode the text: each run of the same character becomes the character followed by the run's length, as in "aaab" to "a3b1".
Return true when every ( [ { in the text is closed by its matching ) ] } in the right order; other characters are ignored.
Return the indices (i, j) with i < j of the first pair, in order of i then j, whose numbers add up to target; none when there is no such pair.
Return true when the two words use the same letters the same number of times, ignoring case.
Return n (1 to 3999) as a Roman numeral.
Flatten the list of lists into one list, in order.
Split the list into chunks of size n (n is 1 or more); the last chunk may be shorter.
Rotate the list left by k places (k is 0 or more and may be larger than the list).
Return the longest text that every word starts with; empty when there are no words.
Return the second largest distinct number in the list, or none when there isn't one.
Merge two lists sorted ascending into one list sorted ascending.
Return the Levenshtein edit distance between the two texts: the fewest single-character insertions, deletions or substitutions turning one into the other.

Write `type Stack { items: [Int] }` with methods `push(self, x: Int) -> Stack` giving a new stack with x on top, `pop(self) -> Stack` giving one without its top item (the same stack when empty), and `top(self) -> Int?`.
Return how many times the character c appears in the text.
Return the median of a non-empty list of numbers: the middle one when sorted, or the mean of the two middle ones for an even count.
Return row n of Pascal's triangle, where row 0 is [1].
Merge overlapping intervals given as (start, end) pairs, returning them sorted by start. Intervals that touch (one ends where the next starts) merge too.
Write a generic function that returns the last item of the list, or `fallback` when the list is empty.
Write a generic function that pairs each item with the next one: [a, b, c] gives [(a, b), (b, c)].
Given `interface Named { fn name(self) -> String }` and the types `Dog` and `Cat` that implement it (both given), write a function returning the names of a list of named things joined by ", ".
Return `part` as a whole-number percentage of `whole`, rounded down. Require that whole is above 0 and part is between 0 and whole, with `require` clauses.
Given `type LoginError = NoSuchUser(name: String) | WrongPassword | Locked(minutes: Int)`, return a message for the error: "no user NAME", "wrong password", or "locked for N minutes".

Given `fn parse_port(text: String) -> Int ! PortError` and `type PortError = Bad(text: String)`, both given, return the sum of the two ports in "A:B" text, passing a failure on with `try`. Text without a colon fails with `PortError.Bad(text: text)`.
Given `type Address { city: String? }` and `type User { address: Address? }`, return the user's city in upper case, or "UNKNOWN".
Sum the squares of 1 to n in two tasks run at the same time (one for the first half, one for the rest), then add their results.

Given `type Item { name: String  qty: Int }`, decode the JSON text into a list of items with `json.decode<T>` and return the total quantity, or -1 when the text doesn't decode. `use std.json` is already there.
Return the total price of the items as an exact `Decimal`: each item is (unit price, quantity).
Given `type Account { owner: String  balance: Int }`, return the account with `amount` added to its balance, using `with`.
Swap the first and last items of the list in place, using an `inout` parameter; a list of fewer than two items stays the same.
Return the keys of the map whose value is at least `min`, sorted.
Return the lines "1. first", "2. second", … for the items, joined with newlines.
Add the two numbers, giving none instead of overflowing.
Return a function that adds `step` to its argument.
Given `type Event = Click | Key(code: Int) | Scroll(dy: Int)`, return how many of the events are key presses.
Return the numbers from 1 to n joined by commas, using a loop that appends to text.
Return the text with every vowel (a, e, i, o, u, either case) removed.
Return true when n is a power of two (1, 2, 4, …).
Return n (0 or more) written in binary, with no leading zeros ("0" for 0).
Return the number that appears most often in a non-empty list; on a tie, the smallest of them.
Build a map from the keys to the values at the same positions; stop at the shorter list.
Given three side lengths, return "equilateral", "isosceles", "scalene", or "invalid" when they can't make a triangle (any side 0 or less, or one side at least the sum of the other two).
Return a list of the lengths of the words in the text (separated by single spaces).
Return how many steps the Collatz sequence takes from n (1 or more) to reach 1: halve an even number, else take 3n + 1.
Return the sum of the digit characters 0 to 9 found anywhere in the text.
Given `type Player { name: String  score: Int }`, return the names of the top k players by score, highest first; ties keep their order.
Clamp every number in the list to the range lo to hi (lo is at most hi).
Return true when the list is sorted ascending (equal neighbours allowed).
Return the color (r, g, b), each 0 to 255, as "#rrggbb" in lowercase hexadecimal.
Simulate a queue of numbers: for each command, a positive number joins the queue and 0 removes the front (when there is one). Return the queue at the end.
